\n", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "To take the long way around"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "To do something quickly or cheaply, often at the expense of quality or safety"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "To follow the rules strictly"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "To be honest and fair"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "2", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

The correct answer is "To do something quickly or cheaply, often at the expense of quality or safety."
\n
\n Key Points

\n\n
    \n\t
  • "Cutting corners" means taking shortcuts or finding ways to do something faster or cheaper. (शॉर्टकट अपनाना या किसी काम को तेजी से या सस्ता करने के तरीके खोजना)
    • \n\t
  • This phrase often implies that the shortcuts being taken may compromise quality or safety.\n\t
      \n\t\t
    • Example: The construction company was cutting corners to finish the project on time.
      • \n\t
    \n\t
    • \n\t
  • The correct answer is Option 2.
    \n\t 
    • \n
\n\n

Additional Information

\n\n
    \n\t
  • Option 1, "To take the long way around," is the opposite of cutting corners and implies taking extra time or effort to do something. (कुछ करने में अतिरिक्त समय या प्रयास लगाना)
    • \n\t
  • Option 3, "To follow the rules strictly," is not related to cutting corners and is actually the opposite behavior. (नियमों का सख्ती से पालन करना ह)
    • \n\t
  • Option 4, "To be honest and fair," is also not related to cutting corners and refers to ethical behavior. (नैतिक आचरण)
    • \n

Key Points

    • \n\t
  • This idiom comes from the practice of citing specific chapters and verses in religious texts to support an argument.
    • \n\t
  • The correct answer is Option 3.
    \n\t

\n\n

Additional Information

\n\n
    \n\t

    • \n\t
  • "Cast pearls before swine" means to offer something valuable to someone who doesn't appreciate it. (किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति को कोई मूल्यवान वस्तु प्रदान करना जो उसकी सराहना नहीं करता)

      The correct answer is "Is the pizza being delivered by you?"
      \n
      \nKey Points

      \n\n
        \n\t
      • The given sentence is in the Present Continuous Tense and in Active Voice.
        • \n\t
      • The rule for changing a Present Continuous Tense from Active voice to Passive voice or Passive to Active Voice:
        • \n\t
      • Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
        • \n\t
      • Structure: \n\t
          \n\t\t
        • Is/am/are + Subject + v1 + ing+ object? (Active Voice)
          • \n\t\t
        • Is/am/are + Object + was/were + being + V3 + by Subject? (Passive Voice)
          • \n\t
        \n\t
        • \n\t
      • Example: \n\t
          \n\t\t
        • Was Esha singing a song? (Active Voice)
          • \n\t\t
        • Was a song being sung by Esha? (Passive Voice)
          • \n\t
        \n\t
        • \n\t
      • The subject of the given sentence is 'you'.​​
        • \n\t
      • The object of the given sentence is 'pizza'.
        • \n\t
      • The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
        • \n\t
      • And 'Is delivering' will be changed into 'is being delivering'.
        • \n\t
      • "Pizza" is a singular subject, so we must "is" with it.
        • \n\t
      • The correct answer is option 4.
        • \n
      \n\n

      Correct sentence: Is the pizza being delivered by you?
